concepts.name_en: Descent Glider: gravity-powered morphing micro-glider follow-cam
concepts.name_zh: 随降滑翔机：靠重力飞行的变形微型滑翔跟拍机
concepts.one_liner: A 95 g folding-wing glider that descends the same vertical drop as the skier, so gravity pays for the flight; it windmills surplus energy into its cell on steep pitches, orbits you at stops and belly-lands in the snow beside you.
concepts.principle: A follow-cam that descends with the skier receives m*g*V*sin(slope) of free power (3.9 W for 95 g at 12 m/s on 20 deg). A light wing needs only D*V. With bird-style sweep morphing (spread for slow, swept for fast), the glide angle stays below typical piste slopes from 6 to 16 m/s, so the propeller is mostly a generator. Camera power, not flight, dominates the energy budget.

architecture.carrier: 95 g EPP/carbon flying wing, span 0.62 m spread / 0.40 m swept (servo sweep), torsion-spring folding wings (loitering-munition style), folding prop on 1S motor that doubles as generator
architecture.support: wing lift; energy from descent (gravity) + 4 Wh Si-anode cell (aerogel-wrapped, self-heating)
architecture.energy: day net 2.6 Wh (advanced) / 2.24 Wh (intermediate) incl. camera; propulsion only 0.99 Wh, regen 0.31 Wh
architecture.sensing: UWB tag on the skier (DW3000 class, 10 cm / +-5 deg) fused with on-board vision + IMU/GNSS; 8x8 ToF for snow-landing flare
architecture.imaging: 4K60 gyro-logging micro camera (no gimbal); Gyroflow-style stabilisation + subject-locked reframing in post; 55 deg output crop
architecture.use_flow: draw from shoulder quiver while skiing >=7 m/s and release -> follow 6-10 m behind/3-4 m above -> orbit at stops -> belly-land 3-5 m downhill-side at end -> pick up, slide into quiver

viewpoints.notes: lags when skier >17.7 m/s (KE cap), catches up when he slows

ops_per_run.ref: 3 ops/run by the strict definition (launch, pick-up, insert); 2 if pick-and-insert counts as one recovery. S2-03 is the fix (1-2 ops, 0 s standstill).

footage.why: Real third-person rear/quarter view at 6-10 m (~330-550 px), smooth because the glider follows a low-passed path; S-turn swings when skier is slow; lags above 17.7 m/s.

interference.why: Nothing on the body but a 1.2 L quiver; no tether, no pull.

convenience.why: ~9 s standstill/run, but 3 ops (launch, pick-up, insert) strict; 51 min/charge.

safety.why: <=14.9 J by design (6.8 J at 12 m/s), no exposed hover rotors, soft EPP; still a flying object over a piste.

simplicity.why: One motor, two servos, no gimbal; fixed-wing pursuit guidance and snow landing are the hard software.

originality.why: No fixed-wing or gravity-powered ski follow-cam found on the market; AER (2016) was a passive thrown glider; round-1 A11 was a 300 g powered wing at 15-25 m with 94 J.

technical_risk.why: Low-Re polar at 95 g, morph mechanism + folding in one airframe, launch in the skier wake.

concepts.bold_hypothesis: On pistes of >=12 deg a <=95 g sweep-morphing glider can follow a skier for a full day on <=1 Wh of propulsion energy, because the descent itself powers the flight.
concepts.falsification_test: (no experiment run) Measure the swept/spread glide polar of a foam prototype by car-roof tow or slope-soaring logs; replay 10 GNSS-logged real runs through the energy model; if propulsion energy >3 Wh/day or L/D(12 m/s, swept) <4, the hypothesis fails.
kill_criteria: Propulsion energy > 3 Wh per 45 filmed min
Snow landing within 5 m of skier < 90 % or damage > 5 %/landing
Subject in frame < 80 % on a tree-lined run (turn radius ~10 m)
Target resorts prohibit all UAS including <250 g follow-me

sim_plan.what_to_model: 3-DOF glider with two-config polar + morph transition, energy state (battery, regen), pursuit guidance with S-turn/height buffer, orbit at stops, snow belly landing, wake-launch release

user_sequence.step: day start: clip 1.2 L shoulder-strap quiver, glider inside (power-on by removal)
push off; at >=7 m/s draw glider from quiver and release overhead (wings spring out, apparent wind = launch speed)
ride: autonomous follow 6-10 m behind/above via UWB tag + vision; regen on steep pitches
mid-run stop: glider orbits r~10 m at 2.4 W (orbit shot), rejoins on restart; no user input
end of run: glider belly-lands 3-5 m to the downhill side; skier slides to it and picks it up
insert tail-first in quiver (wings fold on the tube mouth), board lift
end of day: USB-C charge quiver+glider

concepts.verdict: TOP-1. Physically sound on magnitude; passes KE, endurance, pack, standstill, hands; strict ops = 3 (fix via S2-03 or treat pick-and-stow as one recovery). Regulation: still a UAS (EU C0 follow-me within 50 m is allowed in A1; resort rules decide).

concepts.name_en: VTOL Descent Glider: tail-sitter that hovers only to launch and land on your shoulder
concepts.name_zh: 垂直起降随降滑翔机：只在起降时悬停的尾座式滑翔跟拍机
concepts.one_liner: The S2-01 wing with two small props: it lifts off vertically from a shoulder cradle at a button press, glides down with you (gravity-powered), and hovers back into the cradle when you stop.
concepts.principle: Hover is expensive (13 W) but only needed ~22 s per run; the 150 s of filming is wing-borne and gravity-assisted. Si-anode cells make the hover reserve ~19 g instead of ~40 g, keeping mass at 115 g and KE <=14.9 J up to 16.1 m/s.

concepts.name_en: Skyhook-on-the-move: glider catches a tag line from your pack while you ski
concepts.name_zh: 滑行中天钩回收：滑翔机在滑行中钩住背包拖出的短绳
concepts.one_liner: Insitu SkyHook made personal: in the last 100 m a 1.5 m tag line streams from a pack whip, the S2-01 glider hooks it at 1-2 m/s closing speed and is reeled into the quiver, so you never stop or bend down.
concepts.principle: Glider and skier already move together, so capture happens at closing speed, not flight speed: relative KE 0.03-0.3 J. UWB+VIO relative navigation (~10 cm) suits a hook window of +-0.25 m x 1.2 m.

architecture.support: after capture flies as a mini kite on 1.5 m line
architecture.sensing: UWB anchor pair on the whip (AoA) + glider vision on a high-contrast line marker
architecture.use_flow: button or geofence -> whip+line deploy -> hook -> 3 s reel to dorsal quiver

viewpoints.notes: final approach is itself a dramatic push-in shot

abort_time.ref: skier stops abruptly; glider climbs 0.6 m in that time

footage.why: As S2-01, plus a push-in shot.

interference.why: 1.2 m whip + reel adds ~150 g and a line behind the head for ~10 s.

convenience.why: 0 s standstill, 1-2 ops, no bending in the snow.

safety.why: Glider maneuvers 2-3 m behind the head; 6.8 J ground-frame if the skier stops dead.

simplicity.why: Hook, whip, reel and precision relative guidance.

originality.why: SkyHook is military fixed-pole recovery; no moving-person version found.

technical_risk.why: Skier wake turbulence and line flutter unknown.

concepts.bold_hypothesis: Because both are moving at the same speed, in-motion recovery of a fixed-wing follow-cam is a low-energy docking problem, not a catch problem.

concepts.name_en: Crosswind kite: airborne-wind-energy figure-8 mode keeps the camera kite aloft at slow speed
concepts.name_zh: 侧风飞行风筝：借鉴高空风能的8字飞行让慢速时风筝不掉
concepts.one_liner: Give the round-1 camera kite a 15 g autopilot pod: when the skier slows it flies crosswind figure-8s like an AWE power kite, multiplying its airspeed by ~L/D, so it stays up down to ~2.2 m/s and can sit lower in the wind window.
concepts.principle: Loyd crosswind law: kite airspeed ~ (L/D)*Vw*cos(beta). With L/D 4.4 a 2.2 m/s apparent wind gives the 5.9 m/s the kite needs. When fast, park the kite at the window edge at 35-50 deg elevation instead of 74 deg.

architecture.carrier: round-1 A04 kite 0.30 kg + steering pod (2 bridle servos, IMU)

viewpoints.notes: periodic orbit in footage when in figure-8 mode

concepts.bold_hypothesis: Active crosswind flight removes the kite's low-speed dead zone except at standstill.
